stem: A company has just added several Aurora Replicas to reduce load on its Aurora MySQL primary and wants to confirm the operational steps that let the application benefit safely. Which TWO actions should the team take? (Select TWO.)

choices.text: Promote each new replica to a standalone writer as soon as it is created
Point read-only application traffic at the cluster's reader endpoint instead of each replica
Send a portion of the write traffic directly to one of the new replicas to balance load
Increase the primary instance's storage allocation to make room for the new replicas
Monitor replica lag so read-only clients are not served noticeably stale data

rationale: Routing read-only traffic through the reader endpoint lets the application pick up newly added or removed replicas automatically, and watching replica lag catches the case where a replica falls behind enough to return stale data to a read-only client. Promoting a replica to a standalone writer removes it from the reader pool instead of adding read capacity. Replicas are read-only, so sending writes to one would fail rather than balance load. Aurora Replicas share the primary's storage volume automatically, so the primary's storage allocation does not need to grow just because replicas were added.
